title: SeededRandom must be PCG32 per GDD §13 (currently wraps System.Random) — replay/determinism prerequisite
description: Found during the TASK-025 review: Core's SeededRandom wraps System.Random rather than implementing PCG32, which GDD §13 mandates ('Generador: PCG32... Prohibido System.Random y UnityEngine.Random en Barcade.Core'). System.Random's algorithm is not guaranteed stable across .NET versions, which undermines the §13/D.4 replay guarantee (same seed + inputs => bit-identical session, finalStateHash equality across binary updates on the same contentVersion) and the CI analyzer rule the GDD asks for. Replace the internals of SeededRandom with a proper PCG32 implementation while PRESERVING the public API (NextFloat/NextInt/etc.) so all consumers keep compiling — but note this CHANGES the value sequences for every seed, so any test pinning specific seed-derived values must be updated in the same change (expected churn, do it once, before more mechanics pin more seeds — the longer this waits the more expensive it gets). Add the §13 stream-derivation helpers if absent (sessionSeed -> roundSeed(r) -> per-subsystem streams) since T-108/T-113 will need them. Also add the static-analyzer/CI grep rule §13 requires (no System.Random / UnityEngine.Random in Core). GDD-canonical decision applies. Blocks the fidelity of TASK-032 (.bcrp replay) — that ticket should treat this as a de-facto dependency (comment added there).
acceptance_criteria: SeededRandom is a genuine PCG32 (reference vectors from the PCG paper/site verified by test), public API preserved, all consumers compile unchanged
Seed-pinning tests across the suite updated in the same change; full fast suite green
Stream derivation per GDD 13 exists: sessionSeed -> roundSeed(r) -> named per-subsystem streams, with independence pinned by test (consuming from one stream does not shift another)
A CI/analyzer check fails the build if System.Random or UnityEngine.Random is referenced inside Barcade.Core
Determinism: same seed => same sequence across two process runs (test), documenting the platform scope per GDD 13

comments.author: developer-cloud
comments.body: [developer-cloud] TASK-044 delivered on branch claude/gdd-hito1-cloud, tests-first. 21fe765 test(core): failing spec, red = CS1729/CS1061/CS0117 on the new PCG32 surface (plus the analyzer test genuinely red against the System.Random wrapper). 3fb67ac feat(core): PCG-XSH-RR 64/32 rewrite. Suite 482 -> 492 green. Notes for reviewer: (1) Reference vectors pinned = pcg32_srandom(42,54) canonical demo outputs, recomputed independently from the reference algorithm in this session before pinning (0xa15c02b7...). (2) Public API preserved exactly; SeededRandom(int) maps to (ulong)seed on DefaultStream=54 so the published vectors also pin the int path. (3) NextInt keeps System.Random's edge contract (empty range returns min, inverted throws) and now uses pcg32_boundedrand_r rejection (no modulo bias — new uniformity test). (4) Stream derivation: Derive(sessionSeed, round, RngStream) — SplitMix64 mixes (seed<<32|round) into state, subsystem enum selects the PCG stream/increment; independence pinned by test. RngStream values documented as replay-format-stable (append, never renumber). (5) AC4 analyzer: implemented as an executable fast-suite test that comment-strips every Core/Runtime .cs and fails on \bRandom\b / UnityEngine.Random usage; walks up from the test dir so it also runs under Unity EditMode. A separate CI grep is redundant with this but trivial to add later. (6) Seed-pinning churn was exactly 2 tests (SequencerTests pinned sequences), recalibrated with values computed from the reference algorithm — every other test in the suite was already seed-agnostic (probe-based). (7) Cross-process determinism AC: satisfied by the pinned algorithm vectors (documented in the test header); no subprocess spawning needed. (8) TASK-032 (.bcrp replay) de-facto dependency now satisfied. (9) MicrogameSelector (TASK-035) still uses its own Combine() mixing — migrating it to Derive(...RngStream.Draws) is a 1-line-per-callsite cleanup best done when a ticket next touches it, since it would shift that ticket's statistical corpus.
